Beyond its dangers as an individuated practice, white racial contempt reflects wider patterns of social formation and habits of epistemic deference. To explore these dynamics, the power of active and culpable ignorance is examined through an analysis of epistemologies of resistance. Focusing on resistant forms of racial ignorance permits (1) a robust sense of the interplay between self and social knowledge, (2) a fluid conception of testimonial and hermeneutical injustice, and (3) a dynamic and interactive account of epistemic responsibility. The constructive sections of the chapter explore how racial contempt often emerges in (1) the narration of space, (2) the experience of racial soundscapes, (3) the disavowal of opacity in the interior and social lives of black people, and (4) the politics of self-trust and social suspicion. This chapter shows how viewing racial contempt as an outgrowth of misplaced deference can enrich repertoires of resistance, conceptually and practically. A correlational study of animation narrative style preferences, viewing behavior, and audience experience
G
H
Guofeng Hu
*
School of Arts and Design, Henan Institute of Science and Technology, Xinxiang, China
Article metrics
View details
Abstract
Introduction:
The association between animation narrative styles and the audience’s psychological experience is a critical question in media psychology. Grounded in Uses and Gratifications (U&G), this cross-sectional correlational study examines how narrative preferences are associated with viewing experience.
Methods:
Through a survey of 615 animation viewers, we evaluated how complex/non-linear, coherent/linear, and visual/expressive preferences correlate with cognitive engagement and flow experience. K-Means cluster analysis was utilized for audience segmentation.
Results:
Two significant “preference-experience” pathways emerged: a positive correlation between a preference for complexity and cognitive engagement, and a strong correlation between a preference for coherence and flow experience. Furthermore, viewers were clustered into Analytical Viewers, Casual Plot-Followers, and Indifferent Viewers. Cognitive engagement exhibited a statistical indirect association between complexity preference and flow experience.
Discussion:
These findings supply empirical evidence for understanding audience selection behaviors and offer evidence-bounded implications for content creation and platform recommendation strategies, highlighting an eudaimonic and a hedonic gratification path.

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=autonomous+goal+formation+intrinsic+motivation+objective+discovery&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Evolution of University Students' AI Dependency and Creativity in the Technology Diffusion Process: A Four-Wave Repeated Cross-Sectional Study in China.\", \"abstract\": \"Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping higher education, yet potential risks accompany over-reliance on these tools. Grounded in Rogers' diffusion-of-innovations theory, the present study employed a mixed-methods design. Four waves of independent cross-sectional quantitative data (T1-T4, N = 788) were complemented by semi-structured interviews with 20 undergraduate students. Key patterns emerged as follows: (i) Across later waves, the direct association between external regulation and intrinsic motivation attenuated, while the indirect association operating via identified regulation strengthened. The path from identified regulation to intrinsic motivation was the only relationship that demonstrated significant cross-pair differences while satisfying invariance requirements for all three wave-pair comparisons. Because scalar invariance could not be established, this pattern is interpreted solely as a descriptive group-level temporal trend and should not be read as evidence of intra-individual change. (ii) AI-assisted creativity showed the largest and most consistent downward shift: estimates in later waves were significantly lower relative to the T1 baseline, with effect sizes increasing progressively (Δ = -0.391 to -0.549; d = -0.61 to -0.95; all p < 0.001 following Holm correction). This pattern remained largely unchanged after adjusting for gender, year of study, and academic major, and held up in four predefined subsamples as well as under propensity-score weighting. (iii) The linkage between AI dependency and creativity was significantly positive only at T3 and became negative but non-significant at T4, pointing to a conditional, wave-specific association rather than a stable linear relationship.
